checks.label: It takes 4,200 J to raise the temperature of 1 kg of water by 1 °C: once 1 kg of ice has melted, 4.2 kJ more lifts it to 1 °C and 42 kJ more to 10 °C
Heat of fusion of water is 334 J/g and heat of vaporization 2260 J/g: 1 kg stays at 0 °C until 334 kJ is in, and at 100 °C from 754 kJ until all of it has boiled away at 3,014 kJ

Energy that enters during a phase change causes no temperature change, which is why it is known as latent heat: at every mass, energy put in along either flat line leaves the temperature where it was, and energy put in on the climb raises it
The energy needed depends on the mass, the specific heat capacity and the temperature change: twice the mass needs twice the energy for the same rise, so its line climbs half as steeply
Seawater's specific heat is about 3850 J/(kg C): 2 kg each second warming 10 °C carries 77,000 J each second, which is 77 kW
The heater time is the energy put in over the heater's power: 334 kJ at 3 kW takes about 111 s, and at 1 kW it takes 334 s

Every number the screens print comes from the rule: 420, 588 and 210 kJ; 63 kJ and 4.2 MJ, over 60 times as much; 588 and 1,050 kJ; 48 and 60 °C; 840, 420 and 210 kJ; over five times; 112 s and 12.6 minutes; 900 kJ, about 0.4 kg and 314 °C; 80, 353 and 373 K; 77, 84 and 7.7 kW; 167, 210, 377 and 754 kJ
Each puzzle offers three different answers including its right one, every wrong answer has its own hint, and before Check nothing on its picture shows the answer or a red mark

A wrong pick is drawn in red where it can be: 48 °C and 60 °C off the flat line, climbs that stop at 420 kJ and 210 kJ, a climb on to 314 °C, a bracket for boiling it all away, the slips 588 kJ and 210 kJ, and 353 K and 373 K ringed; a right answer draws no red

A right answer draws the rule's result: 1 kg after 200 kJ still at 0 °C; 2 kg at 100 °C after 840 kJ more; 1 kg still at 100 °C after 900 kJ more, with 0.4 kg boiled away; 0.5 kg at 100 °C after 377 kJ

The graph draws itself from the rule: the curve ends at the dot, it stays at 0 °C while any ice is left, the thermometer reads the same temperature in °C and in K (°C + 273), and the bar's two parts add up to the energy put in
The cup's and the tank's bars share one scale: 63 kJ against 4,200 kJ, so the tank's bar is over 60 times as long
Every demonstration has finished arriving within 4.5 s of its screen opening, none starting before the 0.35 s screen fade ends; every answer's motion, right or wrong, within 2 s
